lines.text: St. Luke 14: 16-24
"A man once gave a great banquet, and invited many; and at
the time for the banquet he sent his servant to say to those who
had been invited, 'Come; for all is now ready' But they all alike
began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a
field, and I must go out and see it; I pray you, have me excused.'
And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to
examine them; I pray you, have me excused.' And another said,
'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.' So the
servant came and reported this to his master. Then the house-
holder in anger said to his servant, 'Go out quickly to the streets
and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor and maimed and
blind and lame.' And the servant said, 'Sir, what you commanded
has been done, and still there is room.? And the master said to the
servant, 'Go out to the highways and hedges, and compel people
to come in, that my house may be filled. For I tell you, none of
those men who were invited shall taste my banquet.? "
My friends, we are all deeply shaken and disturbed by the
news which we have heard this morning. Events have taken
a critical new turn and we are now at war with Russia also.
It was with divided feelings no doubt that we sang our
introductory hymn:
"Hallelujah, Sabbath morn ..•
To-day my anxious cares depart."
For however much we take pains to forget or to surrender to
God our earthly sorrows when we are assembled here in the
house of God, can we forget the heavy burden of anxiety
which lies on all our hearts to-day?
Had I known beforehand in what circumstances I would
have to preach to-day, I would have needed a long time for
reflection on the choice of a text, a text that would contain
an appropriate message for this hour of crisis. As it is, I am
